boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Boston-campus spaces documented by Northeastern’s facilities team for studying, collaborating, or taking a break.

cards.title: Snell Library
cards.subtitle: Library study floors
cards.notes: Choose a floor to match the task, then reserve a room when your group needs a whiteboard or shared display for focused work.
cards.short_summary: A multi-floor library for quiet work, collaboration, and reservable rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern identifies Snell Library as a study hub with different noise levels and spaces for individual work or collaboration.
cards.access_notes: Study-room reservations are available to students during library service hours; check the library booking page before arriving.

cards.title: Curry Student Center
cards.subtitle: Indoor Quad, mezzanine, and game-room area
cards.notes: Use the food-court tables, mezzanine, or first-floor seating for a change of scene; check the directory before heading to a specific floor.
cards.short_summary: A student-life hub with work tables, collaboration seating, and a game-room break option.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern documents study and collaboration seating in Curry’s food-court level, mezzanine, and first-floor common areas, plus a fourth-floor game room.
cards.access_notes: Some spaces host events; consult the Curry directory or posted signage for availability.

cards.title: Churchill Hall
cards.subtitle: Tables near Churchill’s Creations
cards.notes: Set up at a high-top or standard table between classes, especially when you want a seated work spot without reserving a room.
cards.short_summary: An in-between-classes table space in Churchill Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern identifies high-top and regular tables in Churchill Hall as places to study between classes.
cards.access_notes: Use the shared tables considerately and follow any building or dining-area instructions.

cards.title: 300 Massachusetts Avenue
cards.subtitle: Two-level multipurpose study area
cards.notes: Try either level for tables, chairs, or couches when you need a larger shared setting away from the central campus cluster.
cards.short_summary: A two-level, multipurpose study setting near the Prudential area.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern describes 300 Massachusetts Avenue as having two levels of multipurpose rooms and spaces with tables, chairs, and couches for students.
cards.access_notes: This site is a walk from the main campus; verify building access and room availability before traveling over.

cards.title: Northeastern University Law Library
cards.subtitle: Multiple floors of designated work areas
cards.notes: Match your work to the posted noise designation and keep the library’s academic purpose in mind when selecting a seat.
cards.short_summary: A multi-floor library space with different work-area designations.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern describes the Law Library as having multiple floors with different noise levels and areas designated for different types of work.
cards.access_notes: The source notes that the library is primarily used by law students; observe access rules and posted designations.

cards.title: West Village G
cards.subtitle: Lobby and lounge study nooks
cards.notes: Look for the tables and nooks across from the classrooms, and plan to leave before the building’s documented 10 p.m. door lock.
cards.short_summary: A residence-hall lobby and lounge with study tables near classrooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern identifies tables and study nooks in West Village G’s lobby and lounge, across from classrooms.
cards.access_notes: The facilities source states that doors lock at 10 p.m.; comply with residence-hall entry policies.

cards.title: Shillman Hall Lobby
cards.subtitle: Lobby tables and chairs
cards.notes: Use one of the lobby’s tables or chairs for a short work session between classes, keeping pathways clear for people entering the building.
cards.short_summary: A lobby-based work spot with flexible seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern identifies tables and chairs in the Shillman Hall lobby as a place where students can set up to work.
cards.access_notes: This is a shared building lobby; seating availability can vary with class traffic.

cards.title: Law Quad
cards.subtitle: Outdoor space at Huntington Avenue and Forsyth Street
cards.notes: Bring a portable task outdoors and use the seating on a pleasant day; the nearby art, trees, and campus activity make it an open-air pause.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor quad for an occasional study session or reflective break.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern identifies the Law Quad, at Huntington and Forsyth, as an outdoor study spot with art and trees.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor use is weather-dependent; keep personal items attended and follow any campus-event restrictions.

cards.title: International Village
cards.subtitle: Study nooks and tables near the dining hall
cards.notes: Use a nook or table for shared work after a meal or between commitments, while leaving dining and residential traffic routes unobstructed.
cards.short_summary: Nooks and tables in International Village for informal study sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern identifies study nooks and tables in International Village where students can get work done.
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to building access and operational conditions; respect residential and dining-area rules.

cards.title: ISEC Café
cards.subtitle: First-floor café and ISEC lobby seating
cards.notes: Use the first-floor tables or lobby’s sound-canceling chairs for a work block, then move to the patio only when conditions allow.
cards.short_summary: A light-filled ISEC work setting with café, patio, and lobby seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern identifies ISEC Café’s first-floor seating, patio, and nearby sound-canceling lobby chairs as places to work.
cards.access_notes: Café purchases are optional for this seating suggestion; patio access is weather-dependent.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented study environments at Northeastern’s Boston campus, including reservable rooms, silent spaces, and collaboration areas.

cards.title: Snell Library Open Study Space
cards.subtitle: Snell Library • 376 Huntington Avenue
cards.notes: Choose from the library’s soft seating, chairs, tables, and booths; use the setting that fits an individual reading block or a working session.
cards.short_summary: Flexible seating across Snell Library’s open study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Snell Library provides open study space with soft seating, chairs, tables, and booths.
cards.access_notes: Located in Snell Library; follow the library’s current visitor-access policy and code of conduct.

cards.title: Room 255 Quiet Study Space
cards.subtitle: Second floor • Snell Library
cards.notes: Head to Room 255 when it is not occupied by library staff and set up for a designated quiet-study session away from phone calls.

cards.evidence_claim: Room 255 is designated as quiet study space whenever it is not occupied by library staff.
cards.access_notes: Use only when the room is not occupied by library staff.

cards.title: Graduate Study Room 320
cards.subtitle: Third floor • Snell Library
cards.notes: Graduate students can use this silent open-study room for focused reading or writing; keep the glass-enclosed area quiet for everyone working there.

cards.title: Silent Study Room 490
cards.subtitle: Fourth floor • Snell Library
cards.notes: Use Room 490 for silent open study, especially for tasks that benefit from a no-conversation setting such as close reading or drafting.

cards.evidence_claim: Room 490 is a silent open study space available to everyone.

cards.title: Silent Individual Study Rooms

cards.evidence_claim: Silent individual study rooms are located inside Room 490 and are available for reservation during service-desk hours.

cards.title: Snell Library Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Lower level, first, second, and fourth floors
cards.notes: Reserve a group study room before meeting classmates; select a room on the lower level, first, second, or fourth floor that suits the group’s route.
cards.short_summary: Student-reservable group rooms on four Snell floors.
cards.evidence_claim: All students can reserve Snell Library group study rooms on the lower level and the first, second, and fourth floors.

cards.short_summary: Reservable individual rooms on Snell’s upper floors.
cards.evidence_claim: All students can reserve individual study rooms on Snell Library’s second and fourth floors.
cards.access_notes: Reserve during service-desk hours; each student may make no more than three room reservations per week.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Northeastern traditions, from a lucky bronze nose to annual campus rituals and celebrations.

cards.title: Rub King Husky’s nose
cards.subtitle: Ell Hall, Boston campus
cards.notes: Pause at the bronze King Husky in Ell Hall and gently touch its worn nose before an exam; the campus good-luck ritual is especially visible in December.
cards.short_summary: A tactile finals-week superstition centered on Northeastern’s historic husky statue.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern describes touching the nose of the King Husky statue in Ell Hall as a Boston-campus tradition that picks up pace during December finals.
cards.source_title: Rituals, routines and superstitions: How Northeastern students get ready for finals
cards.access_notes: Located inside Ell Hall; follow building-access guidance and do not climb on the statue.

cards.title: Spot the live King Husky
cards.subtitle: Northeastern mascot appearances
cards.notes: Watch university event listings for a King Husky appearance and enjoy the visit from a respectful distance; the live-mascot tradition returned in 2005.
cards.short_summary: Northeastern’s crowned live husky carries forward a mascot lineage begun in 1927.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern reports that the university returned to its tradition of a live mascot in 2005 and that the current King Husky frequently appears on campus.
cards.source_title: The royal history of King Husky, Northeastern’s mascot
cards.access_notes: Appearances vary; treat the dog as a working animal and follow staff direction.

cards.title: Join the “Stacy’s Mom” singalong
cards.subtitle: Northeastern hockey games
cards.notes: At a hockey game, listen for the NU Pep Band’s opening notes and join the crowd’s clean, communal chorus from your seat in the student section or stands.
cards.short_summary: A song-driven arena ritual shared by Northeastern hockey spectators.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern identifies the Pep Band performance of “Stacy’s Mom” and students singing along as a beloved tradition at Northeastern hockey games.
cards.source_title: At hockey games, ‘Stacy’s Mom’ has got it goin’ on
cards.access_notes: Game entry and seating follow the venue’s current ticketing and event rules.

cards.title: Follow the Beanpot run
cards.subtitle: Annual Boston collegiate hockey tournament
cards.notes: Pick a Northeastern Beanpot game to attend or follow, then bring Husky colors and sportsmanship to the annual four-school Boston hockey tournament.
cards.short_summary: Northeastern’s recurring chance to meet its cross-town hockey rivals on a major stage.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern lists the Men’s and Women’s Beanpot among its special traditions and describes the men’s tournament as an annual competition involving Northeastern, BU, BC, and Harvard.
cards.access_notes: Dates, venue, and admission vary by tournament year; consult the current event listing.

cards.title: Form a team for Husky Hunt
cards.subtitle: Resident Student Association annual scavenger hunt
cards.notes: If eligible, organize a team, complete the qualifying quiz, and follow the published rules as clues and creative challenges send teams around campus and Boston.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour Northeastern scavenger hunt built around teamwork, puzzles, and documented safety rules.
cards.evidence_claim: The Resident Student Association calls Husky Hunt its premier annual event: a 24-hour scavenger hunt for undergraduate teams across Northeastern’s campus and Boston.
cards.access_notes: Eligibility, registration, dates, and rules change by year; use the official Hunt site and travel only as its safety rules permit.

cards.title: Mark the end of term at SpringFest
cards.subtitle: Council for University Programs spring series
cards.notes: Check the annual program, choose a performance, lecture, carnival, or concert that suits you, and use the week to close out the academic year with campus programming.
cards.short_summary: A weeklong Northeastern spring celebration organized by the Council for University Programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern describes SpringFest as a week-long program series presented by the Council for University Programs, featuring a major concert, carnivals, and lectures.
cards.access_notes: Programming, venues, and any registration requirements are announced for each year’s event.

cards.title: Wear red and black for Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Annual fall campus celebration
cards.notes: Use the current schedule to choose a Homecoming activity, from Fan Fest to hockey, and share the week with students and alumni while honoring event access rules.
cards.short_summary: A fall reunion ritual that ties campus spirit, alumni, entertainment, and hockey together.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern describes Homecoming Week as a fall tradition with activities that celebrate the university and typically include a major speaker or concert, Fan Fest, and hockey games.
cards.access_notes: Schedules and participation requirements vary annually; check the official Homecoming page before attending.

cards.title: Make a Stuff-a-Husky keepsake
cards.subtitle: Homecoming Week activity
cards.notes: Look for Stuff-a-Husky on the Homecoming schedule, then create a plush Husky keepsake as part of the university’s hands-on school-spirit activity.
cards.short_summary: A Homecoming craft ritual that turns Northeastern’s mascot into a personal memento.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern’s Center for Student Involvement identifies Stuff-a-Husky as a past signature Homecoming Week tradition in which participants stuff a Husky plush keepsake.
cards.access_notes: Listed as a past signature event; availability and supplies depend on the current Homecoming schedule.

cards.title: Attend the Veterans Day ceremony
cards.subtitle: Northeastern University Veterans Memorial, Neal F. Finnegan Plaza
cards.notes: On Veterans Day, gather respectfully at the Veterans Memorial on Neal F. Finnegan Plaza for Northeastern’s annual ceremony honoring members of its community who served.
cards.short_summary: A recurring on-campus observance recognizing Northeastern students, alumni, faculty, and staff who served.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern calls honoring community members who serve or have served in the armed forces a longstanding tradition and holds the ceremony each Veterans Day at its Veterans Memorial.
cards.access_notes: Observe respectfully; confirm the current ceremony time and any weather plan through university event information.

cards.title: Start the semester at Fall Fest
cards.subtitle: Northeastern fall-semester kickoff celebration
cards.notes: Visit Fall Fest to meet student groups and campus teams, catch the entertainment, and use the event as a structured way to find involvement opportunities early in term.
cards.short_summary: Northeastern’s recurring welcome-back celebration combines activities with campus-community discovery.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern describes Fall Fest as a celebration of the start of the fall semester featuring entertainment, games, and opportunities to learn about student organizations, departments, and sports and recreation teams.
cards.access_notes: Consult the current Fall Fest announcement for date, location, access details, and available activities.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Northeastern University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure, under-21-safe first-weekend loop through named campus landmarks, a student hub, arts, study space, recreation, and the nearby transit gateway.

cards.title: 1. Get your bearings at Krentzman Quad
cards.subtitle: 360 Huntington Avenue • campus starting point
cards.notes: Start here and orient yourself to the Huntington Avenue side of campus. Use the quad as a clear meeting point before walking deeper into Northeastern.
cards.short_summary: A named orientation check-in landmark on the Boston campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern’s 2026 orientation information identifies Krentzman Quad at 360 Huntington Avenue as a check-in location.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; confirm any event-specific access separately.

cards.title: 2. Walk the paths at Centennial Common
cards.subtitle: Central campus • outdoor pause
cards.notes: Take a short outdoor reset along the paved paths, then look closely at the commemorative bricks around the common before continuing toward the student center.
cards.short_summary: A campus green with commemorative brick walkways.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern reports that commemorative bricks line the walkways around Centennial Common.
cards.source_title: Northeastern's Boston campus secrets you should know about
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; use normal campus pedestrian access.

cards.title: 3. Find the campus crossroads at Curry
cards.subtitle: Student center • Indoor Quad
cards.notes: Step into the Indoor Quad and Campus Crossroads to get a feel for the building. Check posted programming and services, then choose your next campus stop.
cards.short_summary: Northeastern’s central student-life building.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern describes Curry Student Center as a crossroads for community life and identifies the Indoor Quad as a campus gathering place.
cards.access_notes: Building access and programming can vary; check the student center’s current information on arrival.

cards.title: 4. See what is on at Gallery 360
cards.subtitle: First floor of Curry • 346 Huntington Avenue
cards.notes: While you are in Curry, visit the gallery and spend time with the current exhibition. Check the posted exhibition schedule before making a special trip.
cards.short_summary: A contemporary-art stop inside the student center.
cards.evidence_claim: Gallery 360 is Northeastern’s contemporary art space, located on the first floor of Curry Student Center.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists Monday–Saturday hours of noon–5 p.m.; exhibitions and access may change.

cards.title: 5. Make Snell Library your reference point
cards.subtitle: 376 Huntington Avenue • Boston campus
cards.notes: Walk through the library to identify its study areas and support services. If you need a group space later, use the library’s reservation process during service hours.
cards.short_summary: The Boston campus library and a practical academic anchor.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern identifies Snell Library at 376 Huntington Avenue and notes that student study rooms can be reserved during service desk hours.
cards.access_notes: Check current library hours before visiting; student room reservations are limited to service hours.

cards.title: 6. Cross Library Quad
cards.subtitle: Between Snell and central campus • outdoor connector
cards.notes: Use this named quad as your outdoor connector from Snell toward the rest of campus. Pause to locate the surrounding buildings rather than treating it as a shortcut.
cards.short_summary: A named campus quad shown on Northeastern’s visitor map.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern’s campus map legend identifies Library Quad as a Boston campus destination.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus destination; follow posted campus-access guidance.

cards.title: 7. Spot the history at Matthews Arena
cards.subtitle: 262 St. Botolph Street • athletics landmark
cards.notes: Walk by the arena and note it for future athletics and recreation plans. If open skate interests you, check the current schedule and bring the required identification.
cards.short_summary: A historic ice arena used for Northeastern recreation and hockey.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern calls Matthews Arena the world’s oldest ice hockey arena and offers student-ID-only open skate.
cards.access_notes: Open skate requires a current valid Northeastern ID and a helmet; it is not open to the general public.

cards.title: 8. Check out SquashBusters Center
cards.subtitle: 795 Columbus Avenue • recreation facility
cards.notes: Add the recreation center to your mental campus map. Students interested in squash can review the reservation steps before booking an available court time.
cards.short_summary: A Northeastern recreation center with squash courts and workout stations.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern lists SquashBusters Center at 795 Columbus Avenue with eight squash courts and 52 workout stations.
cards.access_notes: Facility entry requires an active Husky ID for eligible students; squash courts require a reservation.

cards.title: 9. Continue to Carter Playground
cards.subtitle: Beside SquashBusters • Columbus Avenue and Cedar Street
cards.notes: Continue past SquashBusters to see the adjacent athletic complex. Treat it as a future recreation reference point and observe any posted facility rules before using it.
cards.short_summary: A named athletic complex beside SquashBusters.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern identifies Carter Playground as adjacent to SquashBusters and describes it as an athletic complex supporting recreation opportunities.
cards.source_title: Campus hub for club sports and intramurals opens at SquashBusters
cards.access_notes: Use only when public or authorized; follow posted field and playground rules.

cards.title: 10. Finish by locating Ruggles Station
cards.subtitle: Columbus Avenue • Orange Line connection
cards.notes: End the loop by locating the Orange Line entrance for future Boston trips. Save the station as a transit landmark and check the MBTA before relying on a departure.
cards.short_summary: A campus-adjacent transit landmark for future city exploration.
cards.evidence_claim: Northeastern’s 2026 orientation information says the Boston campus is accessible via the MBTA Orange Line at Ruggles station.
cards.access_notes: Transit service and fares vary; consult the MBTA for live service information before traveling.
